title: You Have Five Seconds
summary: Compare what the two pawn captures remove: taking the rook allows promotion, while taking the pawn leaves a rook mate.

nodes.question: What did the earlier rook sacrifice make possible?
nodes.explanation: Begin after ...axb6. Black has captured the rook, vacating a7; White’s pawn on a6 now has an open route to promotion.

nodes.question: What if Black captures White’s a-pawn instead?
nodes.explanation: After ...bxa6 the rook remains on b6. Black’s king on h8 obstructs its own rook’s retreat to h8.

nodes.question: What if Black moved the rook to f7?
nodes.explanation: After ...Rf7 and axb7, White’s pawn on b7 threatens promotion and the rook on b6 remains offered. The earlier eight-piece setup is context.

branches.title: The rook capture clears promotion
commentary: The verified seven-piece starting diagram follows the earlier Rb6 sacrifice. The sacrifice itself belongs to an eight-piece setup and is not encoded here.
a7 uses the open file created when Black’s a7 pawn captured the rook on b6.
Rxh6 takes the other white pawn. The black king on h8 prevents ...Rh8 from blocking promotion.
a8=Q+ promotes with check along the eighth rank.
Kh7 escapes the checking queen and keeps the rook on h6.
Qxb7+ removes the b7 pawn with check. White’s queen against rook and b6 pawn is checked as winning, with further conversion still required.
branches.explanation: Qxb7+ removes the b7 pawn with check. White’s queen against rook and b6 pawn is checked as winning, with further conversion still required.

branches.title: Taking the pawn leaves a mating rook
commentary: This separate seven-piece source diagram follows ...bxa6, which removes the pawn on a6 instead of the offered rook.
Rb8# checks across the eighth rank. Kh8 obstructs ...Rh8, the rook cannot interpose in one move, and the h6 pawn controls g7.
branches.explanation: Rb8# checks across the eighth rank. Kh8 obstructs ...Rh8, the rook cannot interpose in one move, and the h6 pawn controls g7.

branches.title: Capture the rook after ...Rf7
commentary: This seven-piece diagram begins after White’s axb7 in the ...Rf7 variation. It is Black to move; the selected source reply is a capture of the rook.
axb6 captures Rb6 with Black’s a7 pawn. White keeps the pawn on b7.
b8=Q promotes. White’s queen and h6 pawn against rook and b6 pawn is checked as a White win; a quick blitz conversion is not guaranteed.
branches.explanation: b8=Q promotes. White’s queen and h6 pawn against rook and b6 pawn is checked as a White win; a quick blitz conversion is not guaranteed.

exercises.prompt: Why can the rook not simply block on h8?
exercises.answer: The black king already occupies h8. That self-obstruction gives White time to promote with check.

exercises.prompt: Why do the two pawn captures lead to different wins?
exercises.answer: Capturing the rook frees the a-pawn’s file; capturing the a-pawn leaves the rook available for Rb8 mate.

startContext: Begin after ...axb6 at 46 seconds, a supported seven-piece later position. Separate seven-piece diagrams after ...bxa6 at 60s and axb7 at 67s compare the other source branches. The earlier eight-piece Rg6 and Rb6 sacrifices remain context and the exact move tree between these nodes is not asserted.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
sourceCorrections: The caption says the final promoted position is winning for Black. The encoded resulting positions are checked as White wins. Claims about premoving a blitz conversion are not treated as a clock guarantee.
